name: A01: Broken Access Control
evidence: Multiple authenticated API endpoints with user and resource identifier parameters exist (e.g., /api/BasketItems/:id, /api/Addresss/:id, /rest/basket/:id).

name: A02: Cryptographic Failures
evidence: Uses outdated cryptographic dependencies (jsonwebtoken v0.4.0, express-jwt v0.1.3) and contains password/2FA management routes.

name: A03: Injection
evidence: Contains file parsing routes (XML, YAML), search handlers, ORM interactions, and 28 Angular innerHTML/bypassSecurityTrustHtml escape hatches.

name: A04: Insecure Design
evidence: Flaws in high-level control logic and threat modeling cannot be conclusively determined solely from static route tables and package metadata.

name: A05: Security Misconfiguration
evidence: Exposes directory listings (/ftp, /.well-known, /encryptionkeys, /support/logs) and incorporates XML/YAML parsing libraries.

name: A06: Vulnerable and Outdated Components
evidence: Dependency manifest specifies severely outdated packages such as express-jwt ^0.1.3, jsonwebtoken ^0.4.0, and sanitize-html ^1.4.2.

name: A07: Identification and Authentication Failures
evidence: Implements custom authentication routes (/rest/user/login, /rest/user/reset-password, 2FA endpoints) with variable rate-limiting coverage.

name: A08: Software and Data Integrity Failures
evidence: Handlers process untrusted file uploads and structured serialization formats (handleZipFileUpload, handleXmlUpload, handleYamlUpload via js-yaml).

name: A09: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
evidence: Log-serving middleware (/support/logs) and custom metrics collection routes exist without unified logging policy guarantees.

name: A10: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
evidence: Route /profile/image/url executes server-side fetching from user-provided URLs via profileImageUrlUpload.

name: API1: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)
evidence: Exposes auto-CRUD and hand-written REST routes accepting object IDs (/api/Cards/:id, /api/Addresss/:id, /rest/basket/:id).

name: API2: Broken Authentication
evidence: Custom JWT and auth middleware implementations across heterogeneous endpoints (/rest/user/login, /rest/2fa/verify).

name: API3: Broken Object Property Level Authorization
evidence: Auto-CRUD routes bound to database models (User, Product, Card) expose endpoint mutation interfaces without fine-grained field-level schema filters.

name: API4: Unrestricted Resource Consumption
evidence: File uploads (uploadToMemory), product searches, and AI streaming routes lack consistent global rate limits or resource caps.

name: API5: Broken Function Level Authorization
evidence: Administrative and accounting endpoints (/rest/admin/*, /rest/order-history/orders) exist alongside unauthenticated endpoints.

name: API6: Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows
evidence: Automatable business logic endpoints present, including coupon application (/rest/basket/:id/coupon/:coupon), feedback submission, and basket updates.

name: API7: Server Side Request Forgery
evidence: Endpoint /profile/image/url handles remote URL input for image fetching.

name: API8: Security Misconfiguration
evidence: Exposed directory structures (/ftp, /encryptionkeys) and permissive middleware configurations.

name: API9: Improper Inventory Management
evidence: Swagger documentation covers only 1 path, leaving 109 hand-written routes and 28 auto-CRUD endpoints undocumented.

name: API10: Unsafe Consumption of APIs
evidence: Integrates third-party AI completion services (@ai-sdk/openai-compatible) and Web3 smart contracts.

name: LLM01: Prompt Injection
evidence: Detected active LLM chatbot functionality via /rest/chat endpoint with dynamic tool-calling capabilities.

name: LLM02: Sensitive Information Disclosure
evidence: LLM tools execute direct database queries (Sequelize/MongoDB), presenting systemic risks of data retrieval into chat contexts.

name: LLM03: Supply Chain
evidence: Includes third-party AI orchestration dependencies (ai ^6.0.116, @ai-sdk/openai-compatible ^2.0.35).

name: LLM05: Improper Output Handling
evidence: Frontend client uses Angular DOM sanitizer bypasses (bypassSecurityTrustHtml, innerHTML) which can render LLM outputs directly.

name: LLM06: Excessive Agency
evidence: LLM agent is provisioned with autonomous back-end functionality tools including searchProducts, getOrderById, and generateCoupon.

name: LLM10: Unbounded Consumption
evidence: Exposes an LLM interaction surface (/rest/chat) capable of executing database-backed tool calls without dedicated token or request limits.
